source_snapshot.test_set: Intel GNR CPU RAS - Adaptive Double Device Data Correction
source_snapshot.procedure: Enable Spare Interrupt SMI, CE threshold2 and ADDDC; clean baseline/unlock; set dev0 mask0x3; inject two same-location CEs; verify rank count0x2 and overflow; go for SMM; optionally observe copy; verify ADDDC failed/buddy ranks and cleared counter/overflow.
source_snapshot.criteria: Injection succeeds and error logs match.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL but generic logs omit baseline, exact threshold transition, ADDDC region/control and post-sparing clear state.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with CRITICAL risk; preserves the exact two-CE threshold-to-one-bank-VLS state machine and treats copy_in_progress as timing-dependent.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > — Spare Interrupt = SMI • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Correctable Error Threshold = 2 — Trigger SW Error Threshold= Disabled — ADDDC Sparing = Enable • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used to create this recipe. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Halt and confirm there are no preexisting memory related errors on the system. Clear any found error logs or cold boot the system. >>> halt() >>> error.check_mem_errors() a. Considering multiple CECC error injections are performed while halted, the BIOS and OS actions/reporting that would occur if the test were done while the system was running do not occur. One way to modify this test is to inject errors while the system is running to allow the BIOS/OS actions for each CECC error to occur. 3. Check if the injectors are locked for all sockets and unlock if locked. >>> ei.utils.checkInjectorLock(and_unlock=True) 4. Modify memDevs for a single device error injection. Aside from a few DUE patterns and depending on ECC mode, nearly 100% of single device non-permanent ECC errors are correctable. Therefore, dev0msk value can vary and the test will still be valid, but here 0x3 is used to flip bits 0 and 1 on burst 0. This step is optional because the default memDevs will work but this step ensures that any previous memDevs modifications that may have been done do not ruin the test. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=0, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) 5. The hardware per rank CECC error thresholds were set to "2". So inject two CECC errors to the same location to reach the threshold value. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=0, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) 6. Use the following command to verify that the CORRERRCNT counter for that rank has reached the CORRERRTHRSHLD threshold value and that the CORRERRORSTATUS overflow bit for that rank is set. As shown next, the CECC count for rank 0 on MC 0 is 0x2 and that the overflow bit is set. Instead of using the adddc_status_check function, alternative options would be to read the registers mentioned directly or use RAS.mem.memCorrEccCount() so only this table is printed. The adddc_status_check is used because later in the test to verify that the VLS region has been established and it is useful to compare the output of the function from before and after VLS. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0) 7. Resume the system so BIOS can perform its SMM flow and start the VLS sparing operation. >>> go() 8. Optional: You can read the following copy_in_progress bit to check if VLS sparing is in progress. The VLS sparing operation varies in time based on the configuration so this bit may not be seen to be "1" because sparing completed before the CSR was read. >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.sparing_patrol_status.show() 9. Verify that the ADDDC_REGION and ADDDC_REGION_CONTROL registers were modified by BIOS and indicate the failed and non-failed (buddy) ranks. The information printed for the failed bank and device shown next align with the previous error injection. Considering there is only one rank on the channel, the failed and non-failed rank are the same. BIOS selects the buddy bank by flipping bit 0 of the failed bank; in this case, the buddy bank is "1". Also, observe that the per rank CECC counter and overflow bit were cleared. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(0,0)

Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'vls|adddc|corrected|device.data.correction'; echo __ADDDC_VLS_One_Bank_VLS_Region; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

test_case.test_name: One Bank VLS Region — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Trigger the rank CE threshold at one location and verify BIOS SMM establishes one-bank ADDDC VLS with correctly identified failed/buddy ranks and cleared threshold bookkeeping.
required_package: GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS, DIMM rank/bank topology and POR/non-POR approval
Exact source target-to-physical rank/bank/device mapping and mask semantics
Expected count/overflow and ADDDC_REGION/CONTROL failed/buddy fields
SMM completion timeout, serial/OOB recovery and restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Record platform/DIMM and source RAS settings; halt and check clean memory baseline; unlock injectors; set dev0=0 mask0x3; inject exactly two CEs at socket0/ch0/dimm0/rank0/subchannel0/bankgroup0/bank0, reapplying the mask; verify adddc count0x2 and overflow; go once; optionally sample copy_in_progress; verify ADDDC_REGION/CONTROL failed/buddy identities and cleared CE count/overflow; restore and verify health.
test_case.expected_result: Error is injected successfully. Error logs should match.

safety_gate: Dedicated workload-free SUT with live serial/OOB
Reject dirty baseline or mismatched target/mask
Exactly two injections; no attempt to chase the transient copy bit
Stop on wrong counter/overflow, unexpected rank change, hang or incomplete SMM
Preserve state; restore temporary settings and verify memory/OS/BMC health
expected_evidence: Injector unlock, exact mask and two same-coordinate CE transcripts
Post-go ADDDC_REGION/CONTROL failed/buddy ranks/banks and cleared count/overflow
